paragraphs: It is argued that praises should be given to straight-A students, however, some others say no full marks students but improvement students are really deserve. Personally, I think both of them are need to rewarded.

On the one hand, I acknowledged that rewarding to straight-A students is respectable. Since student have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, which in turn propel towards academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition can be easily seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. It naturally follows that students are gradually used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, thereby enabling them to achieve success in later life.

However, I believe that students who show their effortness and improvements should be rewarded. When only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, may cause others to think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. This sense of feeling overwhelmed and disheartened may well gradually lose theirs incentive to study. By contrast, emphasizing improvements may encourage all students to be diligent in their studies as well as help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. Ultimately, the constant desire to outdo themselves, even benefit themselves more than the competitive to win against all others.
In conclusion, I believe that praise should be given to both best and improving students.

paragraphs: Opinions are divided over whether schools should reward students with the best academic results or whether it is more important to reward students who show progress. I believe that both groups need to be rewarded.

On the one hand, I acknowledge that rewarding straight-A students is reasonable. Since those students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage them and other students to study harder, thereby propelling students towards academic gains. Furthermore, competition exists in almost every aspect of life. Becoming familiar with it can help students thrive in the face of fierce competition and may prepare them for success in later life.

However, students who show progress should also be rewarded. If only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, this may cause other students to think that their effort is futile because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel overwhelmed and disheartened and may gradually lose their incentive to study. By contrast, recognizing improvement can encourage all students to work diligently and to keep improving themselves, irrespective of their current performance. Ultimately, the desire to outdo themselves can even benefit them more than competing against others.
In conclusion, schools should reward both students with outstanding academic results and those who make progress.

paragraphs: It is argued that art galleries and museums gradually become useless due to the proliferation of technology. Personally, I am to refute this school of thought.

Admittedly, technology offers flexible culture experience ways. Initially, digital brings many advantages, including high-resolution images; three-dimensional reconstruction; virtual reality platform which enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail whenever and wherever. This can be seen in the way Louvre Museum, renowing the biggest museum in the world, offering a wide range of virtual reality platforms to allow art lovers can pay a visit regardless distance. Therefore, those cannot afford and have mobility issues could be still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I believe that public museums and art galleries still remain integral part of society. Firstly, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person, thus evoking emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, though soldiers' uniform displayed at war museum we can easily immerse in the resistance period and be grateful with suffering society of soldier. Furthermore, museum and galleries attached with vital cultural hubs, thereby symbolizing the identity of a region. Ultimately, becoming a magnet for tourism and fostering a facilitator of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, although benefits of technology should to not cannot be refute, public museums and art galleries still play a pivotal role due to these signature advantages.

Body 1 và kết bài có nhiều cụm chưa thành câu đúng, nhất là 'offering ... to allow ... can', 'could be still access' và 'should to not cannot be refute'. Em cần nghiêm túc viết lại từng câu, nối ví dụ quân phục với sự chân thực và soát động từ trước khi nộp.

paragraphs: It is argued that people can view historical objects and works of art on a computer, making art galleries and museums unnecessary in the future. Personally, I refute this school of thought.

Admittedly, technology offers flexible ways to experience culture and history. Initially, digital technology brings many advantages, including high-resolution images; three-dimensional reconstruction; virtual reality platforms which enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail at any time and from any place. This can be seen in the way the Louvre Museum, a renowned museum, offers online tours that allow art lovers to explore its collections from a distance. Therefore, people who cannot afford a museum visit or have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I believe that public museums and art galleries still remain an integral part of society. Firstly, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. Seeing one in person can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, a soldier's uniform displayed in a war museum helps visitors imagine the resistance period and appreciate the soldiers' sacrifices. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs, thereby symbolizing the identity of a region. It naturally follows that they can attract tourists and facilitate bonding within the community.
In conclusion, although the benefits of technology cannot be denied, public museums and art galleries still play a pivotal role thanks to the direct experience and cultural value they offer.

paragraphs: It is argued that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, while others believe that individuals should be free to take part. I am personally of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited since even a minor error can cause a death of participant. However, I believe that this prohibition sounds unfeasible due to some reasons. Chief of these is that dangerous sports are often held in remote locations, say mountain cliffs, where surveillance still restrict and supervisors cannot throughly follow every individuals. As a result, this prohibition might exist only on paper and even leading to practice underground which harder to ensure basic safety standards.

To add further evidence to my assertion, I note that people should be permitted to do any sport, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. It can be seen in the way almost people engaging with deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping often register in reputable clubs where offers appropriated equipment and qualified supervision. Moreover, newbie is always accompanied by expert who taught them what to do when suddenly accident occur, thereby recognising dangers as well as responding appropriately. Ultimately, through proper training and necessary precautions, these sports may well safer to participation but no activity ensure entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, I believe that this banning is neither practical nor effective, and freedom to choose under strict conditions of training and awareness become a more realistic approach.

Admittedly, opponents of a trial-error approach often point out some reasons that adults should prevent children from making mistakes. Chief of these is that most mistake is avoidable, say, knives, fire or electricity, which are unnecessary to get hurt to learn to be careful. Furthermore, shielding children from harm can forestall mistakes, being a way to fulfill parents’ duty. With pre-emptively helping children, parents may well enjoy a peace of mind, since they do their best to protect and raise their child.

Those on the other side also have their own valid reasonings: Initially, not every parents has the time to supervise children all the time, thereby experiencing with new things as well as making mistake is inevitable. In addition, these invaluable lessons can equip children with practical skills and may stand them in good stead in later stages of life. If children are shielded from everything which labeled as ‘potential dangerous’, they may grow up overdependent on others, shaping undesirable traits.

In conclusion, it seems to me that allowing children to learn from mistakes is the good way to prepare them for the future, provide that parents give guidance on important matters, preventing errors that may derail their future.

paragraphs: Some people believe that children should learn through trial and error, whereas others think adults should help them avoid mistakes. From my perspective, children should be free to make mistakes, provided that the mistakes do not involve serious danger.

Admittedly, opponents of a trial-and-error approach often point out reasons why adults should prevent children from making mistakes. Chief of these is that most mistakes are avoidable; for example, children need not get hurt to learn to be careful with knives, fire or electricity. Furthermore, shielding children from harm can forestall mistakes, thereby fulfilling parents’ duty. By pre-emptively helping children, parents may well enjoy peace of mind, since they do their best to protect and raise their child.

Those on the other side also have their own valid reasons. Initially, not every parent has the time to supervise children all the time, meaning that children will inevitably experiment with new things and make mistakes. In addition, the invaluable lessons from these mistakes can equip children with practical skills and may stand them in good stead in later stages of life. Finally, if children are shielded from everything labelled as potentially dangerous, they may grow up overdependent on others, shaping undesirable traits.

In conclusion, it seems to me that allowing children to learn from mistakes is a good way to prepare them for the future, provided that parents give guidance on important matters to prevent errors that may derail their future.

paragraphs: The given bar chart illustrates how much carbon emissions was emitted from three Fossil Fuels in the UK, over a period of 20 years, commencing from 1990.

Overall, there was an increase in the amount of carbon emission from gas, while the opposite was true in the figures for oil and coal. Also of note is that gas had the highest figures during the period.

To elaborate, in 1990, 230 million tons of carbon emission from gas was released, with a subsequently rise to 300 million tons in 2000. By contrast, the figures for oil and coal decreased, from 270 million tons and 310 million tons to 260 million tons and 250 millions over the same period.

Regarding to the latter half of the provided timeline, the carbon emission from gas went up, from 300 million tons to 320 million tons in 2010. The figures for oil and coal; conversely, went down from 260 million tons and 250 million tons to 210 million tons and 180 million tons respective.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart compares carbon emissions from gas, oil and coal in the UK in five years between 1990 and 2010, measured in millions of tons.

Overall, emissions from gas increased throughout the period and became the highest of the three from 2000 onwards. Coal emissions fell at every recorded point, while oil emissions decreased overall despite a brief rise between 1995 and 2000.

In 1990, coal produced the most emissions, at approximately 310 million tons. Oil accounted for about 270 million tons, followed by gas at around 220 million tons. By 1995, gas had risen to roughly 270 million tons, whereas coal and oil had declined to approximately 280 and 240 million tons, respectively. In 2000, gas climbed further to 300 million tons and overtook coal, which had fallen to around 250 million tons. Oil, by contrast, rose slightly to about 260 million tons.

From 2000 onwards, gas emissions continued to increase, reaching approximately 320 million tons in 2010. Over the same period, oil fell to about 210 million tons and coal dropped to around 190 million tons, making coal the smallest source at the end of the period.

Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.

paragraphs: It is argued that historic subject is one the most important while others believe that science and technology are more pivorle in today's world. Personally, I believe that the comparison between two field of subject is impossible and each subjects had their own benefits that cannot be replaced by another.

On the one hand, historic subject offers students a lot of advantages that cannot be did by science and technology subject. Chief of these is that learning history not only helps students broaden their horizon about their hometown but also helps them acquire knowledge. For example, teaching students about historic figures and historic storytelling can foster students' patriotism and deepen their grateful about their country. Moreover, the priority of science and technology may lead to the lack of patriotism, thereby causing the loss of cultural identity.

On the other hand, subjects like science and technology bring a lot of benefits, which cannot be acquired by historic subject. Initially, science and technology train students about essential skill such as: problem-solving and so on, thus shaping the well-rounded person. Furthermore, science and technology subjects help students become skilled workers in the key economy: doctor, researchers,... that historic subject only allows them to get a jobs related to the field of history.
In conclusion, I believe that both historic subject and science and technology subjects has their own benefits that cannot be replaced by another.

paragraphs.text: People disagree about the place of history in the school curriculum. Some consider it one of the most important subjects, whereas others believe that science and technology deserve greater attention in the modern world. In my view, both areas are valuable because they meet different educational needs, so it is difficult to rank one above the other.

History helps young people understand their society and develop a connection to it. By studying significant events and the people involved in them, students can see how their country was shaped and why certain traditions matter. For example, learning about the sacrifices made during a struggle for independence can deepen their gratitude towards earlier generations. Such knowledge may also encourage them to protect their cultural heritage. If schools neglected history altogether, students might know little about the origins of their own community. This benefit cannot be fully supplied by lessons in science or technology.

Science and technology, however, equip students with practical skills that are increasingly useful in further education and work. Science lessons can teach them to test explanations, interpret evidence and solve problems systematically. Technology classes can help them use digital tools and understand how modern systems operate. A student who develops these abilities may be better prepared for careers in medicine, engineering or research. These subjects can therefore open a broad range of opportunities. At the same time, history should not be dismissed as useful only to future historians: its emphasis on evidence and argument can help students in many professions.

In conclusion, history can strengthen students’ understanding of their past, while science and technology can prepare them for many practical challenges ahead. Since these are distinct benefits, schools should give students a solid education in all three areas rather than treating one as a replacement for the others.
